risks: Current readonly source seams do not implement multiuser row/field authorization; granting read capability or passing readable IDs is insufficient.
Owner cache reuse, average denominator, count/list cardinality, contributor paging and errors can each leak hidden targets independently of sum correctness.

Current allowed shared symbols cannot alone complete transport registration, actual inspector mount, all locale keys and authoritative derived-write rejection; unapproved extra-path edits would violate packet scope.

parseNoteBaseView/isFormula and coercive readField/matchesFilter/compareUnknown can drop new definitions or turn denied/null/list/error into incorrect filters unless accepted prerequisite integration already replaces them.
Shared safe cache cohorts require proof; default actor-scoped keys are necessary but still require current policy/source/query revision fences on cache hits and in-flight responses.

The published Base spec depends on Drive and describes a distinct registered CustomRecord kind/Postgres implementation, whereas LSX design proposes Page content subtype projections. Lead must reconcile accepted canonical authority; this slice must not create a second store to satisfy contradictory historical wording.
Lookup may traverse cyclic graphs or high fanout; reuse bounded evaluator and relation semantics, never recursive unbounded browser traversal or silent truncated aggregate.
Changing checkbox counter meaning to native task relation counts breaks legacy views and can double count promoted tasks.
Remote revoke cannot be learned immediately offline; only accepted lease bounds can authorize cached private values, and reconnect must fence before reading/replay.
Source/spec generation can drift during root-owned uncommitted integration; preflight hashes are historical evidence and must be refreshed on material change.
JSON verifier success proves report lineage/hash integrity only, not actor security, durable native readback, UI, mutation sensitivity or feature completion.
